product_rule: A registered identity is not automatically a public course. Publish a standalone course only when it solves a distinct audience problem, has coherent scope, supported learner claims, a credible assessment path, and a real place in the industry ecosystem.
evidence_inputs: current employer and venue stagehand expectations
Production Atlas research-version production-branch and employer-landscape intelligence
Crew Blueprint course inventory, evidence matrix, historical course bodies, and current publication direction

items.title: Stagehand Fundamentals
items.audience: First-call and early-career stagehands
items.problem_it_solves: New workers do not know what a call will feel like, what information matters, who directs them, how to communicate, or how to be useful without bluffing expertise.
items.why_research_supports_it: Worker discussions repeatedly surface first-call uncertainty, reliability, clarification, call-document literacy, role boundaries, and reputation; current employers independently emphasize punctuality, direction-following, communication, equipment stewardship, and professional conduct.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can describe the call lifecycle, read basic call information, identify the responsible direction path, use listen-clarify-report-back behavior, recognize department boundaries, and explain what reliable stagehand behavior looks like.
items.existing_content_reuse: Current C-SHF-FUNDAMENTALS plus archived 10-module Fundamentals material and First Five Calls material after reconciliation.
items.missing_research_or_content: Direct learner usability testing; employer/lead interviews; editorial simplification; explicit call-document and Preserve-Verify-Report scenarios.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: Foundation awareness only; employer/site rules and qualified specialist authority control specialized work.

items.title: Practical Field Skills Library
items.audience: General stagehands building repeatable ground-level support habits
items.problem_it_solves: Learners need short practical preparation for ordinary assigned tasks without treating each task as a separate major course or implying specialist authority.
items.why_research_supports_it: Workers and employers repeatedly emphasize equipment care, clean handoffs, organization, movement, reset quality, following direction, and preserving existing systems.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can choose a bounded task reference, understand its assignment/authority limits, and connect the task to equipment stewardship and report-back behavior.
items.existing_content_reuse: All 18 current C-FLD-* learner routes and their matrix records.
items.missing_research_or_content: Group navigation; remaining competency-map refinement; Road Case rebuild; consistent owner-review rubric across all skills.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: Library is limited to general-hand recognition and assigned support; hazardous/specialist tasks remain outside learner authority.

items.title: Supporting a Lighting Hang
items.audience: General hands curious about entry lighting support
items.problem_it_solves: New hands need lighting vocabulary, workflow, ownership, and support boundaries without being taught to act as electricians, programmers, riggers, or lighting designers.
items.why_research_supports_it: Community evidence favors useful assigned support over premature technical identity; Production Atlas identifies Lighting as a distinct vendor/role family; employers expect cross-department support under direction.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can recognize common lighting work context, preserve department state, follow an assigned support role, communicate uncertainty, and identify when specialist authority is required.
items.existing_content_reuse: C-LTG-SUPPORT and existing lighting evidence/competency records.
items.missing_research_or_content: Practitioner review for real local-hand expectations; learner usability testing; tone simplification.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: No energized electrical work, temporary-power procedure, rigging procedure, lift operation, programming authority, or independent system changes.

items.title: Supporting an LED Video Wall Build
items.audience: General hands curious about entry video/LED support
items.problem_it_solves: Learners need careful handling, terminology, workflow, and escalation context around video systems without false confidence about processing, networking, structural support, or commissioning.
items.why_research_supports_it: Production Atlas identifies Video/LED as a distinct production branch; worker evidence strongly supports preserving touring systems and following exact assignments rather than silently reorganizing them.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can describe the support workflow at recognition level, protect equipment/state, complete an assigned handoff, and escalate conditions outside the assignment.
items.existing_content_reuse: C-VID-SUPPORT and current video evidence; selected current C2 context may be moved into reference material only after review.
items.missing_research_or_content: Video-lead practitioner review; learner testing; broader role-family context beyond display systems.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: No structural/rigging procedure, powered-access procedure, energized electrical work, processing configuration, networking configuration, or system commissioning.

items.title: Supporting an Audio Load-In
items.audience: General hands curious about entry audio support
items.problem_it_solves: New hands need to understand audio department workflow and handling boundaries without being pushed into console, RF, network, patch-design, or system-tech material too early.
items.why_research_supports_it: Touring-engineer discussions repeatedly value clarification, preserving patch/system ownership, cable/gear care, and hands who execute the requested support rather than trying to prove engineering expertise.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can recognize audio support context, preserve patch/system ownership, perform bounded assigned support, communicate completion, and identify when to defer to audio technicians.
items.existing_content_reuse: C-AUD-SUPPORT and existing audio research/competency material.
items.missing_research_or_content: Audio-head practitioner review; learner usability testing; explicit Preserve-Verify-Report scenarios.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: No console/system configuration, RF coordination, electrical work, rigging, or independent patch/system changes.

items.title: Supporting Staging & Carpentry
items.audience: General hands supporting staging/scenic/carpentry workflows
items.problem_it_solves: Learners need component/workflow literacy and material-support habits while clearly separating carrying/staging support from structural or engineered decisions.
items.why_research_supports_it: Production Atlas separates Staging/Structures and Scenic/Carpentry as real branches; employer material emphasizes load-in/out, stage setup, equipment movement, organization, and authorized assignments.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can recognize common staging/scenic workflow, stage and hand off components as directed, preserve the current plan, and identify decisions requiring responsible structural or department authority.
items.existing_content_reuse: C-STG-SUPPORT plus selected Field Skills and staging/scenic evidence.
items.missing_research_or_content: Practitioner review across staging and scenic contexts; decision whether public label should become Staging / Scenic while preserving existing course identity.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: No structural design, structural acceptance, rigging, automation, powered-equipment operation, or independent assembly decisions.

items.title: Supporting Backline, Props & Wardrobe
items.audience: General hands entering performer-facing support environments
items.problem_it_solves: Learners need strong ownership, state-preservation, discretion, and handoff habits around artist/department-owned items.
items.why_research_supports_it: Community research identifies discretion and respect for other people’s systems as professional expectations; Production Atlas identifies Backline as a distinct role/vendor family with artist-area professionalism.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can recognize ownership-sensitive work, preserve arrangement/labels/state, ask before changing department-owned items, and complete discreet handoffs.
items.existing_content_reuse: C-BPW-SUPPORT plus current C2 as a research/module pool, not automatic public continuation.
items.missing_research_or_content: Targeted interviews with backline, props, and wardrobe practitioners; determine whether deeper material should split by department.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: Support does not authorize tuning, repair, adjustment, alteration, powered operation, or other department-owned specialist decisions.

items.title: Move a Road Case With a Partner
items.audience: General stagehands
items.problem_it_solves: Road-case movement is common but easy to teach too generically without accounting for team communication, route conditions, equipment ownership, and site-specific constraints.
items.why_research_supports_it: Employers and workers repeatedly emphasize case movement, equipment stewardship, teamwork, and staying within the assigned task.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can describe a bounded partner-movement assignment, communicate the handoff, and identify when route/equipment conditions require stopping and asking.
items.missing_research_or_content: Owner field-context interview and bounded rebuild already requested.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: No powered equipment, vehicle loading, ramp/traffic decisions, or site-specific movement method beyond authorized direction.

items.title: Over-Under Cable Coiling
items.audience: General stagehands handling cable under direction
items.problem_it_solves: Poor cable handling creates rework and damages trust even when the worker knows more advanced technical vocabulary.
items.why_research_supports_it: Touring/local-crew discussions repeatedly cite cable handling and preserving looms/patch state as basic reputation signals.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can explain the approved coiling concept, preserve labels/looms/state, and ask before altering a department-owned cable arrangement.
items.missing_research_or_content: Consistency check against department-specific cable ownership language.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: No disconnecting, repatching, energized electrical handling, or altering touring looms without responsible direction.

items.title: Ratchet Straps Under Direction
items.audience: General hands assigned non-specialist strap support
items.problem_it_solves: Learners need to recognize the task and its authority boundary without inferring rigging, fall-protection, lifting, or cargo-plan competence.
items.why_research_supports_it: Field practice includes assigned strap work, while both current course notes and specialist-boundary research require strict separation from qualified decisions.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can identify an assigned support role and when the responsible person must specify or verify the application.
items.missing_research_or_content: Owner review for wording and scenarios.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: Not lifting/rigging/fall-protection/cargo-plan authority; exact use and acceptance stay with the responsible current authority.

items.title: Flatbed Cargo-Securement Support
items.audience: General hands assisting an authorized load lead/driver
items.problem_it_solves: Workers may assist around cargo without understanding that securement planning and legal acceptance belong elsewhere.
items.why_research_supports_it: Logistics is a distinct Production Atlas branch; current course notes already preserve driver/load-lead/regulatory authority.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can describe a bounded support role, preserve the load lead’s plan, and escalate uncertainty rather than making acceptance decisions.
items.missing_research_or_content: Continued legal/regulatory source freshness and practitioner review.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: Driver/load-lead/regulatory acceptance and vehicle operation remain external.

items.title: Barricade Setup Under Direction
items.audience: General hands assigned barricade support
items.problem_it_solves: Barricade work can be mistaken for generic assembly even though the exact system and event/site plan control configuration and acceptance.
items.why_research_supports_it: Site operations and barricade vendors are distinct Production Atlas functions; current course notes already preserve exact-system and event-plan authority.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can recognize the assigned support role and identify when system/site instructions or responsible personnel control the next step.
items.missing_research_or_content: System/vendor practitioner review before any detailed revision.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: No crowd-safety design, structural acceptance, layout authority, or substitution for the current event/barricade plan.

items.title: Cable Ramps & Protectors
items.audience: General hands assigned cable-route protection support
items.problem_it_solves: A simple-looking task intersects with approved routes, egress, accessibility, pedestrians, and vehicle traffic.
items.why_research_supports_it: Employer and worker evidence values route care and site organization; current course notes already require exact product/route/interface review.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can recognize route-protection support, preserve the approved route, and escalate conflicts rather than redesigning the route.
items.missing_research_or_content: Accessibility/egress/traffic interface review as claims change.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: Approved route, product, accessibility, egress, and traffic plan control placement and acceptance.

items.title: Team Lift, Carry & Set Down
items.audience: General stagehands
items.problem_it_solves: Workers need a common communication and handoff model for team movement without encouraging strength demonstrations or unsafe improvisation.
items.why_research_supports_it: Community evidence criticizes showing off strength/speed and employers repeatedly require teamwork and safe movement assistance.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can describe coordinated assigned movement, communication, and stop/ask behavior when the task exceeds the crew or conditions.
items.missing_research_or_content: Detailed competency-map refinement.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: No mechanical lifting, powered equipment, rigging, or task-specific load acceptance.

items.title: Cart, Dolly & Hand-Truck Movement
items.audience: General stagehands
items.problem_it_solves: Common equipment movement needs route awareness, control, teamwork, and equipment care rather than speed-first behavior.
items.why_research_supports_it: Employers explicitly mention carts and equipment movement; worker evidence values clean material flow and staying within assignment.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can recognize a bounded cart/dolly assignment, communicate route conflicts, and protect equipment and surrounding work.
items.missing_research_or_content: Detailed competency-map refinement and owner scenarios.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: Does not authorize forklifts, powered pallet equipment, vehicle operation, or traffic-control decisions.

items.title: Cable Deployment & Gathering
items.audience: General stagehands
items.problem_it_solves: Cable movement creates rework when hands ignore routing, labeling, ownership, or the department’s existing plan.
items.why_research_supports_it: Touring-worker evidence repeatedly emphasizes clean cable work and not altering looms/patches without instruction.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can support cable movement while preserving route/label/system state and asking before changing the plan.
items.missing_research_or_content: Detailed competency-map refinement.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: No energized electrical handling, patch changes, traffic-route design, or department system changes without responsible direction.

items.title: Case & Boneyard Organization
items.audience: General stagehands
items.problem_it_solves: Poor case/boneyard organization slows load-ins/outs and makes crew search for gear or hands.
items.why_research_supports_it: Worker and employer evidence strongly values equipment stewardship, organization, storage, and staying findable.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can maintain an assigned organization scheme, preserve labels/ownership, and report exceptions rather than inventing a new system.
items.missing_research_or_content: Detailed competency-map refinement.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: Venue/tour/site storage plan and traffic/emergency access requirements remain controlling.

items.title: Work-Area Reset & Handoff
items.audience: General stagehands
items.problem_it_solves: A task is not complete when tools, gear, damage, missing items, or unfinished work are left ambiguous.
items.why_research_supports_it: Current employer descriptions explicitly require restoring spaces, returning equipment, and reporting damage or unfinished items; community evidence treats clean handoffs as a reputation signal.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can restore the assigned area to the current plan, account for items, and report completion/exceptions to the responsible person.
items.missing_research_or_content: Detailed competency-map refinement; integrate Preserve-Verify-Report language.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: Reset does not authorize repair, reconfiguration, or alteration of specialist systems.

items.title: Ground-Level Soft Goods
items.audience: General stagehands assigned ground-level drape/soft-goods support
items.problem_it_solves: Learners need handling/ownership awareness without drifting into overhead rigging or system-specific installation authority.
items.why_research_supports_it: Field Skills evidence and staging/scenic role taxonomy support ground-level recognition and assigned support.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can identify a bounded ground-level support role, protect material condition, and defer system/overhead decisions.
items.missing_research_or_content: Detailed competency-map refinement and system-specific review where claims are added.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: No overhead rigging, fire-treatment decisions, structural decisions, or specialized installation authority.

items.title: Pipe-and-Drape Support
items.audience: General stagehands assigned ground-level pipe-and-drape support
items.problem_it_solves: A common event task needs bounded component recognition and support while exact systems and site conditions vary.
items.why_research_supports_it: Production environments frequently use temporary scenic/event systems; Rhino and community evidence both stress context variation and scope awareness.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can recognize components and follow the responsible person’s current system plan without substituting another method.
items.missing_research_or_content: Detailed competency-map refinement; manufacturer/system review for any detailed claims.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: Exact system, stability/ballast, egress, fire-code, and acceptance decisions remain with current responsible authority.

items.title: Riser & Deck Component Support
items.audience: General stagehands assigned material/component support
items.problem_it_solves: Learners need to distinguish moving/staging components from structural assembly, configuration, and acceptance.
items.why_research_supports_it: Production Atlas separates staging/structures from general logistics; the strategic safety boundary explicitly keeps structural assembly procedural training out of novice content.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can support component flow and recognize when configuration/acceptance belongs to authorized staging personnel.
items.missing_research_or_content: Detailed competency-map refinement and staging-practitioner review.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: No structural configuration, assembly acceptance, engineering, rigging, or system substitution.

items.title: Basic Tool Recognition & Handoff
items.audience: General stagehands
items.problem_it_solves: New workers benefit from recognizing ordinary tools and making clean handoffs without treating a tool list as authorization to operate every tool.
items.why_research_supports_it: Beginners repeatedly ask what tools matter, while employer and safety evidence make assignment, training, and context more important than carrying advanced gear.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can recognize common tool families, confirm what is requested, hand tools off cleanly, and identify when operation requires training/authorization.
items.missing_research_or_content: Detailed competency-map refinement and employer-context wording.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: Recognition/handoff does not authorize powered, cutting, electrical, access, or other hazardous tool operation.

items.title: Jobsite Tape, Label & Marking
items.audience: General stagehands
items.problem_it_solves: Labels and marks are part of another crew’s information system and can create errors if changed casually.
items.why_research_supports_it: Worker evidence strongly supports preserving touring labels/looms/state and current employer evidence values documentation and organization.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can recognize an assigned marking/label task, preserve existing information, and confirm before changing or removing marks.
items.missing_research_or_content: Detailed competency-map refinement.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: Do not remove safety/engineering/system labels or alter another department’s state without current responsible direction.

items.title: Scenery, Flat & Wagon Movement
items.audience: General stagehands assigned scenic movement support
items.problem_it_solves: Scenic movement needs coordination and ownership awareness without drifting into structural, fly-system, automation, or changeover authority.
items.why_research_supports_it: Production Atlas identifies Scenic/Carpentry as a distinct production branch; employers commonly expect general stagehands to support scenery movement under direction.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can support assigned scenic movement, preserve current marks/ownership, and stop when conditions exceed the assignment.
items.missing_research_or_content: Detailed competency-map refinement and scenic-practitioner review.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: No fly-system, automation, structural, rigging, or powered movement procedure.

items.title: Dock, Ramp & Trailer Handoff
items.audience: General stagehands working around loading areas
items.problem_it_solves: Loading areas combine equipment flow with vehicles, ramps, traffic, forklifts, and changing authority boundaries.
items.why_research_supports_it: Production Atlas identifies Logistics as a distinct branch and current employer descriptions emphasize docks, loading, carts, team movement, reporting, and authorization.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can describe the handoff and communication role around an assigned loading flow and recognize when vehicle/traffic/equipment authority lies elsewhere.
items.missing_research_or_content: Detailed competency-map refinement; loading-dock practitioner review.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: No vehicle driving, forklift/powered equipment operation, traffic control, ramp acceptance, or cargo-plan authority without applicable authorization.

items.title: How Live Production Fits Together
items.audience: New and early-career workers confused by industry structure
items.problem_it_solves: Learners see job titles and festival brands but cannot tell who produces the event, who hires labor, how departments connect, or why authority changes by context.
items.why_research_supports_it: Career/navigation is the strongest sampled audience need; Production Atlas shows a multi-employer ecosystem across labor, venues, vendors, touring teams, site ops, logistics, and production offices.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can navigate a branching role/employer map, distinguish common production branches, and identify likely hiring/authority relationships without assuming one universal ladder.
items.existing_content_reuse: Fundamentals department overview, Production Atlas production-branches.js, employer landscape, IATSE/venue/vendor research, existing role-map backlog.
items.missing_research_or_content: Cross-context role-family map validated by workers in venue, touring, festival, corporate, theatre, union and non-union environments.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: Role map describes pathways only; it does not confer titles, appointment, qualification, or authorization.

items.title: Finding Work & Building Professional Trust
items.audience: Stagehands trying to get first calls, callbacks, department opportunities, or touring/vendor connections
items.problem_it_solves: New workers hear vague advice to network but do not understand actual labor/vendor/venue entry paths or how ordinary work behavior becomes referrals.
items.why_research_supports_it: Community evidence repeatedly links progression to reliability, referrals, specialization, and reputation; Production Atlas shows stagehand entry is commonly through labor providers, locals, venues, and vendors rather than the festival brand itself.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can identify realistic work-source categories, explain professional trust accumulation, maintain truthful experience records, and choose a next department/employer research path.
items.existing_content_reuse: Archived Fundamentals career module, Roadmapdev discovery, Production Atlas employer/market intelligence.
items.missing_research_or_content: Direct labor-coordinator interviews and current-market usability testing.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: No employment guarantee, earnings promise, or claim that networking substitutes for required qualifications.

items.title: Touring & Festival Work Reality
items.audience: Local workers considering festival or touring work
items.problem_it_solves: Public-facing live events can hide irregular schedules, travel, seasonality, downtime, close crew environments, changing sites, and lifestyle demands.
items.why_research_supports_it: Community discovery repeatedly raises travel, fatigue, laundry/personal organization, seasonality, work-life sustainability, and the difficulty of moving from local work into touring; Production Atlas describes seasonal and vendor-mediated labor.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can describe realistic differences between local, festival, venue, and touring work and identify personal/logistical questions to resolve before pursuing a path.
items.existing_content_reuse: Roadmapdev touring/festival discovery and Production Atlas festival labor/employer research.
items.missing_research_or_content: Touring-crew and festival-worker interviews; learner decision-usefulness testing.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: High-level work-life and career literacy only; no medical treatment advice or hazardous-work procedure.

items.title: Worker Business & Admin Basics
items.audience: Event workers navigating pay, records, engagement types, expenses, or contractor/employee terminology
items.problem_it_solves: Irregular work creates confusion around timekeeping, rates, scope, payment terms, expenses, records, and changing legal/tax concepts.
items.why_research_supports_it: Community research repeatedly surfaces pay/admin friction and inconsistent work; Production Atlas warns that stagehand engagement may be W-2, union referral, staffing payroll, vendor payroll, contractor, volunteer, or unknown depending on context.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can keep basic work records, distinguish common engagement labels from legal conclusions, identify questions to ask about a call, and locate current authoritative resources when legal/tax rules matter.
items.existing_content_reuse: Existing career/admin research identities, archived Fundamentals career material, Production Atlas engagement-type model.
items.missing_research_or_content: Current jurisdiction-aware legal/tax source framework and professional review of final wording.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: General literacy only; no individualized legal, tax, payroll-classification, or financial advice.

items.title: Training, Credentials & Specialist Paths
items.audience: Workers deciding how to progress beyond general stagehand support
items.problem_it_solves: Learners do not know which credentials, employer training, union pathways, specialist education, or external qualifications matter for a chosen role.
items.why_research_supports_it: Career questions repeatedly ask which credentials matter; Rhino stresses scope and qualified guidance; Production Atlas separates rigging, power/electrical, department vendors and IATSE contexts; Crew Blueprint already holds substantial ETCP/ESTA/OSHA research.
items.learning_outcome: Learner can distinguish general experience, employer training, role appointment, certification/credential, and specialist qualification, then locate the current external authority for the path they want.
items.existing_content_reuse: ETCP/ESTA/OSHA source records, Production Atlas IATSE/role research, Rigging/Electrics archived research as awareness-only source material.
items.missing_research_or_content: Current credential/source freshness registry and role-family validation across markets.
items.external_qualification_or_safety_boundar: Explicitly does not teach rigging, energized electrical work, temporary-power tie-ins, work-at-height, structural assembly, powered-equipment operation, pyro, lasers, or other hazardous procedures.

non_public_reclassification_direction.course_2_and_course_3_material: Reconcile into MODULE, REFERENCE, SPECIALIST_AWARENESS, ADVANCED_OWNER_REVIEW, or future course candidates; do not preserve an arbitrary three-course ladder.
non_public_reclassification_direction.lead_material: Keep Lead / Crew Chief Foundations as an advanced owner-review candidate; treat department Lead bodies as reference packs until role/appointment/practitioner validation supports publication.
non_public_reclassification_direction.supervisor_material: Reframe toward production coordination / operational responsibility; do not present Supervisor as a universal rung.
non_public_reclassification_direction.rigging: Awareness, role map, qualification context, stop/escalate behavior, and external training only for beginner-facing Crew Blueprint.
non_public_reclassification_direction.electrics_and_production_power: Awareness, role/authority boundaries, and qualification context; do not use advanced load-planning material as a missing Course 1 substitute.
non_public_reclassification_direction.infrastructure_and_internal_research: Keep retrievable for agents/Owner Review; redistribute useful concepts into guides or references rather than public course tiles.
non_public_reclassification_direction.historical_variants: Preserve for lineage and salvage review; do not count alternate presentations as new learner products.

conversion_assessment.public_catalog_and_navigation: low_complexity; largely completed in the v2-preserving client layer
conversion_assessment.fundamentals: moderate; strong existing body, but needs humanization, call-document scenarios, audience-fit audit and learner testing
conversion_assessment.field_skills: low_to_moderate; routes exist, but grouping, competency refinement and several owner/practitioner reviews remain
conversion_assessment.department_starters: moderate; five live Course 1 routes can be reused but need audience-fit, practitioner and owner review
conversion_assessment.career_resource_guides: moderate; research substrate exists but five coherent public guides still need writing and review
conversion_assessment.course_2_course_3_reclassification: moderate_to_high; requires claim-level salvage and assessment/source reconciliation
conversion_assessment.lead_supervisor_reconciliation: high; historical bodies are valuable but role structure is context-specific and requires practitioner validation
conversion_assessment.rigging_electrics_specialist_domains: high; authority/safety boundaries require strict external qualification and current-source review
conversion_assessment.full_143_identity_reclassification: moderate_to_high structural/editorial task; preserve IDs and lineage while assigning each identity one primary product classification
